primitives.name: Data Quality Score
primitives.verbatim_quote: t("lower confidence when data quality is poor (stale, thin market)", () => { const base = scoreGame(makeOddsInput()); const withBadContext = scoreGame(makeOddsInput({ context: { bookmakerCoverageMax: 2, dataFreshnessMinutes: 200, // very stale hasSpreadMarket: true, hasTotalMarket: false, hasH2HMarket: false, }, })); const baseConf = base.find((p) => p.pickType === "SPREAD")?.confidence ??
primitives.latex: DQ = f(Cov, Fresh, H2H, Sp, Tot)
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Cov': 'Bookmaker coverage count (dimensionless)', 'Fresh': 'Data freshness in minutes (time)', 'H2H': 'Presence of head-to-head market (binary)', 'Sp': 'Presence of spread market (binary)', 'Tot': 'Presence of total market (binary)', 'DQ': 'Data quality score (0, 1)'}
primitives.assumptions: Assumes higher coverage and recent data increase confidence, while missing key markets decrease it.
primitives.breakdown_regime: DQ saturates to minimum when all inputs are absent.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's conformal prediction framework where DQ acts as a weight in uncertainty quantification.
layer2.telemetry: Observed drop in predictive accuracy when Fresh exceeds threshold and Cov is low.

primitives.name: Uncertainty Penalty
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'DQ': 'Data quality score (0, 1)', 'Consensus': 'Market consensus percentage (0, 1)', 'U': 'Uncertainty penalty factor (0, 1)'}
primitives.assumptions: Higher uncertainty (low DQ or low Consensus) increases penalty, reducing adjusted confidence.
primitives.breakdown_regime: U approaches 1 when either DQ or Consensus is minimal.

layer2.mapping: Derived from GSE's state-transition logic where U modulates transition probabilities based on information asymmetry.
layer2.telemetry: Correlated with increased betting volume imbalance when U exceeds empirical threshold.

primitives.name: Batch Game Scoring
primitives.verbatim_quote: import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest"; import { americanToImpliedProbability, removeVig, clamp, scoreGame, scoreGames, }
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Score_i': 'Individual game score (arbitrary units)', 'S': 'Aggregated batch score (arbitrary units)'}
primitives.assumptions: Linear aggregation is valid under independent scoring components; non-linear interactions require additional weighting.
primitives.breakdown_regime: S collapses to zero when all Score_i are neutral.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's ensemble learning methodology where S represents posterior probability after observing multiple bets.
layer2.telemetry: Tracking S's distribution reveals clustering patterns that indicate market inefficiencies.

primitives.name: American Odds Conversion
primitives.verbatim_quote: import { describe, it, expect } from "vitest"; import { americanToImpliedProbability, removeVig, clamp, scoreGame, scoreGames, }
primitives.assumptions: Standard vig of 10% for -110 odds; conversion assumes linear relationship between odds and probabilities.
primitives.breakdown_regime: P_{implied} diverges when A approaches extreme values (e.g., +10000 or -1000).

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's probability calibration step where P_{implied} feeds into state-action value functions.
layer2.telemetry: Monitoring conversion error bounds helps calibrate GSE's internal belief states against external prices.
